Reproduced at HEAD in Chromium (verify/f5.js). The page's measure() passes no seg options, so it runs refine 2. A median-soldier sheet with a 2,000 px figure (4479x2320, the spec minimum) takes 16,271 ms on the main thread; the same sheet with refine 0 takes 1,668 ms. At 3,000 px (6718x3480) it takes 24,980 ms, against 3,957 ms without refinement. At 390 px with 4x CPU throttling (verify/f5t.js), the 2,000 px sheet takes 44,418 ms. These times are a little inflated, because Node jobs ran alongside the first run. The refinement changes this clean sheet's score by only 0.2% (26.95 against 27.01). pushPull allocates Float32Array(w*h*3), about 125 MB at this size, plus W and the pyramid levels. Results are correct, but the tab is frozen for 16-44 s on its intended input, long enough for the browser's unresponsive-page prompt. I did not reproduce an out-of-memory crash.
verdicts.better_fix: Limit refineMask to each view's bounding box plus a margin, or to a band about 4 px wide around the coarse mask's edge, instead of the whole image. For example, crop img and mask to the union of the splitViews boxes padded by 2*refineDist, refine the crop, and paste it back. Or run Measure.measureSheet in a Web Worker built from a Blob of the inlined measure.js source; it has no DOM use. Either way, keep 'Measuring…' with elapsed time in #toolStatus.

verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced at HEAD through the page's #file input (verify/make_odd.js, verify/ui.js). A black figure on a fully transparent background (alpha-black.png) gives 'No result: Found 0 view(s); a sheet needs a front and a side view (and ideally a back view).' A grey-120 figure on grey 150 (lowcontrast.png) gives the same message. loadFile (app.html:1505-1508) draws onto a transparent canvas, and segment() ignores alpha, so transparent pixels read as RGB 0,0,0: black on black.
